text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
NASA BORBA

- Montenegro cannot return to the IMF and the World Bank independently from Yugoslavia because international organisations deal only with sovereign states, Montenegrin Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic was told in Washington.

- The post of Yugoslav National Bank governor is expected to be filled by April 15 and the most serious contender is Investbanka director Nikola Stanic. The post has been vacant since May 1996 and the function discharged by deputy governor Bozidar Gazivoda.
- Germany is ready to extend trade facilties to Yugoslavia, visiting new Belgrade mayor Zoran Djindjic was told.
- A panel discussion on information law to be held Thursday evening in the Serbian parliament with the participation of all parliamentary parties and live coverage.
- Serbian information minister Radmila Milentijevic is satisfied with the strong response to the draft information law because the whole of Serbia is taking part in the dialogue.
- Events in Albania are directly linked to the Kosovo issue. Its weakening represents a blow to the Kosovo question, says vice-president of the Parliamentary Party of Kosovo (PPK) Bajram Kosumi.
- Yugoslavia cannot sell one million tonnes of surplus corn from last year's sowing because the price of domestic corn is higher than corn on world markets.

- Association of primary agricultural producers Jugoagrar asks Yugoslav parliament to pass a law turning farmers' debts into a public debt failing which Serbian farmers will block main roads and border crossings from 12-17 hrs local time on March 19.
POLITIKA
- Serbian government says all conditions met for spring sowing and funds secured for payment of last year's crop.
- European Union Ministerial Council meeting on March 24 will also discuss the return of Yugoslavia to the World Trade Organisation and of its trade preferentials.
- Names of 38 members of Belgrade University Council appointed by Serbian government published in the Official Gazette.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI

- The Yugoslav interior ministry is drafting a law on dual citizenship between Yugoslavia and Croatia which is expected to be completed in two months. Biggest problem is where military service will be served.
- The new federal cabinet is expected to be extended to 15 instead of the present 11 ministers, the composition will be announced at the federal parliament session on March 20
- Families of Yugoslav diplomats in Albania evacuated.
POLITIKA EKSPRES
- Yugoslavia closes border crossings with Albania, only crossing open is Bozaj in Montenegro.
DNEVNI TELEGRAF
- Serbs from Kosovo were not invited to attend the Serbian-Albanian intellectuals' round table to be held on Mt Brezovica, Kosovo, from March 21 to 23. -- Belgrade newsroom +381 11 2224305
